report:
The argument establishes its claimed P19.1 classification for actual canonical finite-energy weak rays on a connected smooth compact Kähler manifold. The datum, probability entropy, squared-log time, initial-point requirements, and extended-value cases are specified. P19.2–P19.4 are unclaimed and remain unresolved by this submission.

The normalization is consistent. With dd^c=i∂∂̄/(2π) and t=−log|τ|², the inner boundary flux is −rF_r/2=F_t. The conversion to MP's logarithm convention scales the background class and divisorial datum together. The resulting mixed slopes have no additional factor two. The discrepancy used for entropy is A_X=A_{X×P¹}−1 on normalized Gauss valuations, giving the coefficient (a_i+1−b_i)/b_i and A_X(v_triv)=0.

The singular mixed-slope passage is valid. Ordered energy gives equation (5); the Hölder pairing estimate has positive exponent 2^(−n), while the other energy bounds grow only linearly in time. Dividing first by time and then taking the decreasing approximation limit removes the error. Signed smooth inputs can be expressed through positive inputs on a fixed common model. The corresponding finite-energy estimates also establish continuity of the fixed twisted pairings used later.

The log-canonical volume proof retains the nonreduced multiplicities. Its independent radial variables occupy the weighted simplex ∑b_i y_i≤t+O(1), whose volume is O((1+t)^p), p≤n. The finite branching in the dependent coordinate does not change this bound. Ambient differential wedges have bounded coefficients against the logarithmic frame, proving the claimed fiber-volume domination. Entropy duality and the directed discrepancy supremum therefore prove the lower bound, including infinite non-Archimedean entropy.

For model rays, the divisor-removed complex Hessian bound implies domination of the restricted positive current on every noncentral fiber. Restriction is legitimate because the residual potentials are continuous; the current inequalities restrict to the fibers. Bedford–Taylor continuity gives the determinant domination in (9). The bounded density then yields (10), and the calibrated pairing and lower bound give the exact model entropy slope.

Appendix A supplies the needed discrepancy gate. At a Rees prime, the finite normalization map has tangential rank N−1 on the reduced generic divisor. Coordinate and generator-ratio functions consequently provide the required independent restricted differentials. The pulled-back determinant has exact order m−1, while its base coefficient has order at least m−N(m−ℓ). Thus k_F+1≤N(m−ℓ). This argument does not require normal injectivity into the base. The derivative–multiplier inclusion is valid after retaining the codimension-two condition; removing the integral divisorial factor preserves the order difference. Nonexceptional primes and dimension one are also treated.

The special Fujita application uses the transcendental paper 2609.31089v1, rather than importing the catalogue's polarized theorem into a larger setting. Its vertical equivariant construction applies in dimension n+1. The uniform regularization loss is independent of the varying coefficients; the fixed-chart comparison underlying this assertion was checked in Popovici's proof. Orthogonality in the central locus follows from restricted-volume vanishing together with the central restricted/global product identity. The divisor inequality 0≤Δ_k≤K_{Y_k/Xcal} is correct for an SNC reduced support, including nonreduced fibers. Consequently the canonical-error limit, not merely volume convergence, controls the additional entropy. This proves model energy-and-entropy recovery. No automorphism assumption from Trusiani's Theorem A is needed. [Transcendental Fujita source](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.31089v1).

Joint continuity uses genuine common upper maximal rays. Equations (17)–(19), the ordered metric identity, and affine energies give fixed-time d_1 convergence uniformly on bounded intervals. The finite-entropy-start argument then takes the approximation limit at fixed time through the lower-semicontinuous convex Mabuchi functional. It does not assume entropy continuity for arbitrary strong sequences. Subtracting the finite twisted-energy slope proves the required upper bound.

The arbitrary-ray cases are established, rather than assumed. Linear upper growth follows from the constant-speed d_1 property and the integral/supremum bounds for normalized psh functions. The increasing multiplier caps retain every divisorial coefficient: subadditivity gives dyadic decrease, and the cap −m tends to −∞. The cap rays dominate the original ray, providing a uniform lower energy bound and hence finite energy of its actual datum. Equation (22) identifies maximality with zero energy defect.

The local difference-integrability proof applies without projectivity. Noncentral multiplier ideals are trivial because finite-energy slices have zero Lelong numbers. At the center, invariant multiplier ideals are determined through their valuative data; local Bergman generators then give exponential integrability for every exponent. Fubini produces the sequence used in (23), and the full energy supporting inequality supplies bδ−1. The entropy slope already exists because the twisted-energy slopes are finite and Mabuchi is extended convex after any finite-entropy slice. Thus positive defect forces infinite slope. Rays with no finite-entropy slice have infinite entropy identically. Fixed time translation preserves the datum, and the energy-defect argument establishes maximality of the tail.

Both P¹ examples are valid. The stationary bounded potential has singular angular Monge–Ampère measure and infinite entropy at every slice, although its datum and non-Archimedean entropy are zero. It therefore justifies the exceptional branch without excluding arbitrary initial points. The second example gives entropy slope 1 and energy slope −1/2 in the declared convention.

Harmless clarifications: “affine time shift” in the datum definition should read “addition of an affine function of time”; the calibration example's “weights one and zero” are Monge–Ampère component masses, while its datum values are −1 and 0. Also, the older BFJ valuative theorem is stated with J_+; identification with J uses strong openness. Adding that precise citation completes the already stated multiplier-ideal foundation and introduces no new hypothesis. [BFJ](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0702487), [Guan–Zhou](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.7158).

The result exceeds the catalogue's smooth polarized maximal-ray scope: it allows nonprojective compact Kähler manifolds, arbitrary E¹ starting points, nonmaximal rays, and infinite-entropy starts. The finite-slice condition selects a branch of an exhaustive classification; it is not an additional assumption on the target domain.
premises: On smooth compact Kähler (X,α), MAα:E¹_NA,sup→M¹_α is a strong homeomorphism; Eα(ψ)≤Eα(φ)+∫(ψ−φ)MAα(φ) for φ,ψ∈E¹_NA. Fixed smooth cohomological mixed energies extend continuously in the strong topology. [MPWN, Theorem B and §§2.3,5](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2509.09442v1).

On smooth compact Kähler (X,α), weak φ_j→φ with bounded Jα(φ_j) implies ∫|φ_j−φ|MAα(ψ)→0 for every ψ∈E¹_NA. The quasi-metric ∂α(φ,ψ)=Jα(φ,ψ)+|supφ−supψ| induces strong convergence. [MPWN, Lemma 5.0.5 and Theorem 5.2.2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2509.09442v1).

For a dominating SNC model Y of smooth compact Kähler (X,α), real vertical D and f_D≥1, set A=ρ_X*α, Γ=A+D and C_Y=K_Y/(X×P¹)+B_red−B. Then Eα(Pαf_D)=Vol(Γ)/((n+1)V), Hα(Pαf_D)=⟨Γ^n⟩·C_Y/V, and ⟨Γ^n⟩_Y|E=⟨Γ^n⟩·E for central components E. [MPWN, Propositions 9.1.2–9.1.5](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2509.09442v1).

For smooth compact Kähler (X,α) and φ∈E¹_NA with Hα(φ)<∞, real PL obstacles f_j exist with Pα(f_j)→φ strongly and Hα(Pα(f_j))→Hα(φ). [MPWN, constructive proof of Theorem 9.2.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2509.09442v1).

On compact Kähler X, a linearly growing p_X*ω-psh ray has a unique PSH_NA datum determined by divisorial coefficients. NA psh functions admit decreasing model approximation. For equivariant SNC retractions, A_X=sup_Y(A_X∘r_Y), monotonically under domination, and A_X(v_E)=(ord_E K_Y/(X×P¹)+1−b_E)/b_E. [MP, §§3.2,4.3 and Theorem 5.1.4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2409.06221v2).

For compact Kähler (X,ω), w∈E¹(ω) and φ∈E¹_NA(α), there is a unique maximal ray r(w,φ), order-preserving in both arguments, with initial point w and datum φ. In MP's matched conventions its energy is E(w)+sEα(φ). [MP, Theorem 5.1.7 and Theorem 5.3.4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2409.06221v2).

For compact Kähler X, mean-normalized U_i,V_i∈E¹(ω), and smooth closed η_i, the mixed-pairing difference is bounded by C(n)A(max_i Jω(U_i,V_i))^q(max_i{Jω(U_i),Jω(V_i)}+Tω)^(1−q), where q=2^(−n), A=V∏_i(1+2∥η_i∥ω), and Tω is the uniform supremum-minus-mean bound. Pairings are continuous along decreasing finite-energy limits. [MP, Lemma 5.3.2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2409.06221v2).

In Li's smooth polarized projective framework with smooth reference initial potential, an E¹ ray U and its associated maximalization satisfy exp(b(Û−U))∈L¹(X×Δ) for every b>0. Its proof is local; MP transports the local argument to compact Kähler manifolds in Proposition 6.3.1. [Li, Lemma 3.1 and Remark 3.2](https://sites.math.rutgers.edu/~cl1412/papers/maximal.pdf), [MP](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2409.06221v2).

Let Xcal be a smooth compact Kähler equivariant configuration dominating X×P¹, D real vertical, f_D≥1, and Γ=ρ_X*α+D big. There are smooth equivariant modifications p_k:Y_k→Xcal with vertical centers and effective vertical real E_k such that β_k=p_k*Γ−E_k is Kähler, β_k^(n+1)→Vol(Γ), β_k^n·K_Y_k/Xcal→0, and β_k^n·p_k*ξ→⟨Γ^n⟩·ξ for every fixed smooth closed real (1,1) class ξ. [Trusiani, Theorem B, Lemmas 3.4–3.5 and §5](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.31089v1).

On a fixed compact Kähler manifold, if ∑c_jθ_j+dd^c u≥−cω with smooth closed θ_j, c_j>0 and c>0, then u has an analytic-singularity replacement of type (J(u),1) satisfying ∑c_jθ_j+dd^cũ≥−(c+A)ω, with A depending only on the fixed forms and ω, not on u,c,c_j. [Trusiani, Lemma 4.3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.31089v1); the coefficient-independent fixed-chart comparison is [Popovici, Lemma 1.2](https://comptes-rendus.academie-sciences.fr/mathematique/item/10.1016/j.crma.2003.11.011.pdf).
For a big real (1,1) class γ on a compact Kähler N-fold Z and a prime divisor F⊂EnK(γ), the restricted positive volume ⟨γ^(N−1)⟩_Z|F is zero. [Vu, Theorem 1.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2307.15909).

A smooth relatively Kähler cohomological test configuration dominating X×P¹, with X compact Kähler, admits from every smooth Kähler initial potential a unique compatible weak ray whose divisor-removed total potential has locally bounded complex Hessian. [Sjöström Dyrefelt, Lemma 4.6 and Remark 4.7](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1601.07659v2).

For every u∈E¹ on a compact connected Kähler manifold, there are smooth Kähler potentials u_j with d₁(u_j,u)→0 and Ent(MA(u_j)|ω^n/V)→Ent(MA(u)|ω^n/V), including extended infinite values. [Berman–Darvas–Lu, Lemma 3.1 with f=0](https://msp.org/gt/2017/21-5/gt-v21-n5-p08-s.pdf).

On a compact connected Kähler manifold, the Chen–Tian expression for Mabuchi extends to E¹ as its greatest d₁-lower-semicontinuous extension and is convex along canonical finite-energy geodesics. Smooth contracted energies are d₁-continuous; for positive contraction forms they are convex along bounded-complex-Hessian geodesics. [Berman–Darvas–Lu, Propositions 4.4–4.5 and Theorem 4.7, with zero twist](https://msp.org/gt/2017/21-5/gt-v21-n5-p08-s.pdf).

On compact Kähler (X,ω), canonical E¹ weak geodesics are constant-speed d₁ geodesics with affine normalized energy E. For a,b∈E¹, I₁(a,b)=∫|a−b|(MA(a)+MA(b))≤C d₁(a,b); if a≥b, d₁(a,b)=E(a)−E(b). Energy obeys E(a)−E(b)≤∫(a−b)MA(b) and is continuous under decreasing E¹ approximation. [Darvas, Theorems 4.17,5.5, Corollary 4.14 and energy formulas](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1409.2072v2).

On a compact Kähler manifold, every E¹ potential has zero Lelong numbers, its Monge–Ampère measure charges no pluripolar sets, and E¹⊂L¹(MA(v)) for every v∈E¹. [Guedj–Zeriahi, Corollary 1.8, §4.1 and Theorem 4.2 with p=1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0612630v2).

A psh germ with zero Lelong number has exp(−b u) locally integrable for every finite b>0. The same conclusion holds after adding a smooth local background. [Skoda, Proposition 7.1](https://www.numdam.org/article/BSMF_1972__100__353_0.pdf).

For a psh germ u on a smooth complex germ, its valuative transform determines J_+(u) through L²(û)∩O=J_+(u). For every divisorial valuation, the normalized orders of J(mu) converge to the corresponding generic Lelong coefficient of u. [Boucksom–Favre–Jonsson, Theorem 5.5 and §5](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0702487).

For every psh germ u, J(u)=J_+(u)=⋃_{ε>0}J((1+ε)u); equivalently, local integrability of |f|²e^(−u) implies local integrability of |f|²e^(−p u) on a smaller neighborhood for some p>1. [Guan–Zhou, Theorem 1.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.7158).

For psh u on a bounded pseudoconvex coordinate ball, the weighted Bergman space with weight e^(−m u) generates J(mu). On relatively compact subdomains, finitely many such generators f_i yield B_m=m^(−1)log∑|f_i|² with B_m≥u−C_m/m; each |f_i|²e^(−m u) is locally integrable. [Demailly–Kollár, Theorem 4.2 and its finite-generation argument](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/9910118).

For psh functions u,v on a complex manifold, analytic multiplier ideals satisfy J(u+v)⊂J(u)J(v). In particular J(2mu)⊂J(mu)². [Demailly–Ein–Lazarsfeld, Theorem 2.6(ii)](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0002035v2).

For a coherent ideal a on a smooth complex manifold and a log resolution π with a·O_Y=O_Y(−D), its exponent-one multiplier ideal is π_*O_Y(K_Y/Z−D). Hence multiplication by an integral effective Cartier divisor G gives J(a·O(−G))=J(a)·O(−G). [Ein–Lazarsfeld–Smith–Varolin, §4 log-resolution formula](https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~dror/paper-jump.pdf).

Mixed Bedford–Taylor products of locally bounded psh potentials are well-defined, symmetric and multilinear, and converge weakly when each potential decreases to a locally bounded psh limit. [Bedford–Taylor, Theorem 2.1 and Corollary 2.2](https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~ebedford/PapersForM655/BTNewCapacity.pdf).

For a compact Kähler manifold (X,ω), every ω-psh function is the decreasing limit of smooth ω-psh functions; the approximation can be made strictly ω-psh by the usual vanishing rescaling. [Błocki–Kołodziej, Theorem 1](https://gamma.im.uj.edu.pl/~blocki/publ/appr.pdf).

[Demailly–Kollár, Theorem 4.2 and its finite-generation argument](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/9910118).

For psh functions u,v on a complex manifold, analytic multiplier ideals satisfy J(u+v)⊂J(u)J(v). In particular J(2mu)⊂J(mu)². [Demailly–Ein–Lazarsfeld, Theorem 2.6(ii)](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0002035v2).

For a coherent ideal a on a smooth complex manifold and a log resolution π with a·O_Y=O_Y(−D), its exponent-one multiplier ideal is π_*O_Y(K_Y/Z−D). Hence multiplication by an integral effective Cartier divisor G gives J(a·O(−G))=J(a)·O(−G). [Ein–Lazarsfeld–Smith–Varolin, §4 log-resolution formula](https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~dror/paper-jump.pdf).

Mixed Bedford–Taylor products of locally bounded psh potentials are well-defined, symmetric and multilinear, and converge weakly when each potential decreases to a locally bounded psh limit. [Bedford–Taylor, Theorem 2.1 and Corollary 2.2](https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~ebedford/PapersForM655/BTNewCapacity.pdf).

For a compact Kähler manifold (X,ω), every ω-psh function is the decreasing limit of smooth ω-psh functions; the approximation can be made strictly ω-psh by the usual vanishing rescaling. [Błocki–Kołodziej, Theorem 1](https://gamma.im.uj.edu.pl/~blocki/publ/appr.pdf).
